chunks: And recite to them the story of Noah,
when he said to his people: 'O people,'
if my staying with you and my reminding you of the signs of Allah is burdensome to you,
then upon Allah I have placed my trust.
So gather your affair and [call] your associates,
then let not your plan be obscure to you,
then pass your sentence against me and give me no respite.
ai.seo_question: What did Noah say to his people when they found his message burdensome?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) demonstrates the Shia virtue of *tawakkul* by inviting his people to consolidate their power and allies, challenging them to execute their plan without delay. This rhetorical challenge underscores his confidence that divine decree would prevail over their collective schemes, a theme echoed in the narrative of the Prophet Muhammad's confrontation with the Quraysh.
